name: Lambda AI cloud GPU instances (NVIDIA H100 SXM, self-serve)
region: US-based (Lambda does not itemise regions on the pricing page)
price_basis: per GPU-hour, 8-GPU instance (208 vCPU / 1800 GiB / 22 TiB SSD): H100 SXM $3.99; A100 SXM 80GB $2.79; A100 SXM 40GB $1.99; B200 SXM6 $6.69; V100 $0.79. Smaller shapes are dearer per GPU: 4x H100 $4.09, 2x H100 $4.19, 1x H100 SXM $4.29, 1x H100 PCIe $3.29, 1x GH200 96GB $2.29. Quote is '+ applicable sales tax/VAT/GST'. Fetched 2026-10-03.
notes: THE CHEAPEST CREDIBLE ON-DEMAND H100 HOUR ON A DEDICATED 8-GPU NODE IN THIS SLICE: $3.99/GPU-hour against $6.88 on AWS p5 and $11.06 on Google a3 - about 42% under AWS and 64% under GCP. Self-serve, first-come, no sales call, which also makes it the best-evidenced record here after the hyperscaler APIs. A counter-intuitive and useful detail: on Lambda the per-GPU price FALLS with node size ($4.29 single, $4.19 dual, $4.09 quad, $3.99 octuple), so take the 8-GPU node - the opposite of GCP G2, where the small node is cheaper. If you only need one H100, the PCIe single at $3.29 is the cheapest single H100 in the slice. Two caveats. (1) The 1-Click Cluster tiers are a DIFFERENT and more expensive product: H100 at $6.16/GPU-hr for 16 GPUs, $5.85 at 64, $5.54 at 256, all quote-only via a sales call - so 'Lambda H100' is ambiguous between $3.99 self-serve and $6.16 clustered, and the clustered number is worse than AWS p5 on-demand. Quote the Instances price, not the Clusters price, unless you need the colocation. (2) lambdalabs.com/service/gpu-cloud/pricing is a 404 - the live page is lambda.ai - so old links and blog posts citing the old domain are stale. No published commitment discount: reserved capacity is a sales conversation.
